html:
A stone tower in Gyeongju, South Korea, built in the reign of Queen Seondeok of Silla (632 to 647). Its name means star gazing tower, and it is often called the oldest surviving astronomical observatory in East Asia.

The tower is a bottle shape about nine metres high, made of some 360 stones, with a square window halfway up and a square frame on top. People seem to have climbed in through the window by ladder. Many see symbols of the calendar in its stones, but such counts are debated, and some scholars think it was more a ritual or symbolic structure than a working observatory.

Either way, it shows the weight Silla put on watching the sky, which mattered for calendars, farming and omens about the ruler. It stands among the royal tombs of Gyeongju, Silla's capital, which later became the seat of Unified Silla.
